trivia_fact: Azure launched in February 2010 as "Windows Azure," emphasizing its Windows Server heritage. Microsoft renamed it to "Microsoft Azure" in April 2014 to reflect its growing support for Linux and open-source workloads, which now make up over half of Azure VMs.

Azure's compute fabric runs on a customized version of Windows Server with the Hyper-V hypervisor. Over time Microsoft developed a minimal "Azure Host OS" stripped down from full Windows Server, optimizing for cloud workload density and security.

Azure DevOps has had four names: Team Foundation Service (2012), Visual Studio Online (2013), Visual Studio Team Services (2017), and finally Azure DevOps (2018). Each rename reflected Microsoft's shifting brand strategy from developer tools to cloud platform.

Azure operates in more regions than any other cloud provider, with 60+ announced regions across 140+ countries. Microsoft leveraged its existing global datacenter footprint from Xbox Live, Office 365, and Bing to expand Azure's physical presence rapidly.

The Azure CLI (az) is written entirely in Python and is open source on GitHub. This was a deliberate choice for cross-platform compatibility. It replaced the older Node.js-based Azure CLI (azure-cli, later called "classic CLI") which was retired.

Azure Active Directory was renamed to "Microsoft Entra ID" in July 2023. Despite the rebrand, engineers worldwide still call it "Azure AD" or just "AAD." The rename was part of Microsoft's push to unify identity products under the Entra brand family.

Microsoft acquired GitHub for $7.5 billion in 2018, surprising many given Microsoft's historical antagonism toward open source. Under Microsoft ownership, GitHub Actions launched, Copilot was born, and the platform grew from 28 million to over 100 million developers.

Azure Cosmos DB evolved from DocumentDB (2015) and was rebranded in 2017. It offers turnkey global distribution with five consistency models ranging from strong to eventual — more granularity than any competing managed database service.

Microsoft invested over $13 billion in OpenAI and became its exclusive cloud provider. Azure OpenAI Service lets enterprises access GPT models with Azure's compliance and networking controls — making Azure the default cloud for many AI workloads.

Microsoft's CEO Satya Nadella declared "Microsoft loves Linux" in 2014, a dramatic reversal from Steve Ballmer calling Linux "a cancer" in 2001. By 2019, Linux VMs surpassed Windows VMs on Azure, and Microsoft even ships a custom Linux distro (CBL-Mariner/Azure Linux) for its own infrastructure.
